key_insight: Variational quantum classifiers showed a trade-off between circuit expressivity and training stability, but classical models remained superior on synthetic network traffic.
engineering_relevance: For similarly structured anomaly-detection tasks, classical baselines remain the practical choice, while quantum circuit design and optimizer selection warrant careful testing.
method: Generated synthetic network traffic for anomaly-detection evaluation.
Compared four VQC architectures with varied encodings, ansatz circuits, quantum neural network types, and optimizers.
Benchmarked quantum models against Support Vector Machine and Random Forest classifiers.
evidence_signal: VQC-4 reached up to 89.0% accuracy, VQC-3 was identified as best overall using ZFeatureMap, RealAmplitudes, and ADAM, and classical baselines achieved perfect classification on the synthetic data.
watch_item: Synthetic-data results do not establish real-world utility or quantum advantage; deeper circuits were training-sensitive, and VQC-2 produced many false negatives.
paper_title: Quantum Anomaly Detection in network traffic using Variational Quantum Classifiers
